svg.title: From job post to recruiter e-mail
svg.desc: From job post to recruiter e-mail. Step 1, Bring in job posts (lead-fetch / lead-import): Parsers pull out the role, company, location and years (and skills, from the feeds and Naukri). Only LinkedIn posts carry a recruiter e-mail. A repost (same e-mail, same role) is stored once. Step 2, Keep what fits (lead-filter): Every dropped lead gets a reason code. Each kept lead gets a 0-100 fit score with its matched skills, and a link where the source gives one. Step 3, Build the brief (lead-draft-packet): Your facts file is the only source of your claims. Keep it outside the repository; jw reads it from the path you pass each time and stores neither the file nor the path. Step 4, Write the e-mail (Claude): Claude writes the subject and body from the packet when you ask it. Nothing is sent here. Step 5, Check the draft (lead-draft-submit): The draft is ready or blocked, with reasons. A lead with no recruiter e-mail is blocked as no_contact: apply through its link, or the Naukri invite, instead. Step 6, You approve a batch (lead-approve): Your approval is the only way a draft becomes sendable. Drafts that are not ready are skipped with a reason. Step 7, Send once (lead-send): Each approval is spent once. A resume that changed since approval is refused before Gmail is called. Step 8, Confirm and follow up (lead-reconcile / mail-sync): Unknown sends are matched in your Sent folder by recipient, subject and the X-JW-Action-Id header. mail-sync reads replies and bounces.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: What jw does today, one step at a time. jw and its database run on your machine; Claude reads the packet when it writes; no e-mail is sent until you approve.
